what_i_found.the_builders_causal_claim_is_wrong_and_s: The status file says level-up's D2 fell because 'fixing the collision removes the overlapping-ink pixels that were inflating round 4's number'. It cannot: D2 is the cardinality of a set of pixels, and two glyphs on one pixel make it differ ONCE — collapsing columns can only shrink the union, separating them can only grow it. Measured on the two arms with byte-identical panel rects and the same row rects: 95.7% of the 0.0335 fall is inside the ten attribute rows, and the solid-trough (gauge) columns collapse 918 -> 551, a 40% cut, which is exactly progress.js moving the gauge from r[2]*0.64 (156 units) to r[2]-gaugeX0-10 (72 units). Level-up clears the floor by 0.0022 because its gauge is half as long, not because its screen got fuller. S58's RULING is untouched and correct; its stated MECHANISM is not what happened in round 4 either — the 0.0910 -> 0.1855 rise was the DENOMINATOR falling 5.1x (57.2% -> 11.1% of frame). Filed as an arbitration_question, not as an edit.
